title: Files & Storage says 'Last backup: Never' while Settings > Advanced > Backup & Restore says a real timestamp
summary: Closed before this wave, and I re-proved it rather than trusting the claim. The page no longer reads the raw autoSaveServiceProvider: auto_save_settings.dart:169 watches autoSaveLifecycleProvider (auto_save_service.dart:785-810 — the only thing that loads the persisted autosave.* keys and calls start(config, lastBackup)), and auto_save_settings.dart:192-193 reads `ref.watch(autoSaveStatusProvider).valueOrNull ?? service.status`, where autoSaveStatusProvider (auto_save_service.dart:762-778) backfills lastBackup from BackupService.lastBackupSettingKey = 'autosave.last_backup_at' (backup_service.dart:166) — literally the same key Backup & Restore reads at backup_screen.dart:432. The live repro predates the fix: the verifier's screenshots under /tmp/ns-audit/shots are all stamped 2026-08-03 16:42-17:10, while auto_save_settings.dart was rewritten at 2026-08-04 01:45. WHAT I ADDED: the previous test could not fail on a single-line revert, because the two paths are redundant and either one alone renders the truth — so a refactor could delete one silently and leave the card one edit from lying again. Two new cases isolate them.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/auto_save_settings_hydration_test.dart -> 'truthful with only the lifecycle-hydration path' (silences autoSaveStatusProvider with a never-emitting stream, so only the hydrated service can produce '2h ago') and 'truthful with only the persisted-key backfill' (overrides autoSaveLifecycleProvider with an un-started service — the backend-swap orphan — so only the autosave.last_backup_at backfill can). 5/5 green.
revert_check: TWO separate reverts, each failing its own case only. (1) auto_save_settings.dart:192-193 `ref.watch(autoSaveStatusProvider).valueOrNull ?? service.status` -> `service.status`: 'truthful with only the persisted-key backfill' FAILED ('Found 0 widgets with text "2h ago"'), other 4 passed. (2) auto_save_settings.dart:162-172 `ref.watch(autoSaveLifecycleProvider).when(...)` -> `_buildConfigured(context, ref.watch(autoSaveServiceProvider))`: 'truthful with only the lifecycle-hydration path' + the two schedule cases FAILED. Restored -> 5/5 pass.
caveats: test/screens/settings/captures_landscape_test.dart fails on 2 golden pixel comparisons. Pre-existing Windows-captured goldens on Linux, and not mine: the same captures_landscape_test.dart fails identically under test/screens/diagnostics (2) and test/screens/guiding (3), neither of which this wave touched. Those files are @Tags(['golden']) and are excluded from the melos gate by design; the full skotiq_app suite run the way the gate runs it (`flutter test --exclude-tags golden`) is 2818/2818 green with every change in this report applied.

title: Timezone picker is inert: every displayed time silently stays on the host's timezone
summary: The picker itself and the dashboard/status-bar faces were closed in earlier waves (location_settings.dart:453 offers only kUtcOffsetTimezones, which clock_provider.dart:219 parses; status bar temperature_and_time.dart:161, dashboard header dashboard_header_actions.dart:105, night timeline night_timeline.dart:42, moon card moon_card.dart:38, command-bar chip command_bar.dart:568 all read clockProvider). Three surfaces were still host-local, and the largest is the one this defect is ABOUT: the planetarium Tonight tab is a page of nothing but site facts. FIXED HERE: (1) tonight_tab.dart — all 8 twilight faces, moonrise/moonset, the best-target transit and the 3 satellite-pass faces went through DateFormat('HH:mm').format(x.toLocal()); they now go through a single _siteHhmm(x, clock) fed by ref.watch(clockProvider), and _SatellitePassCard takes the Clock as a REQUIRED parameter so the next caller cannot silently default to host-local. (2) altitude_chart.dart — the Rise/Transit/Set chips, the time axis and the touch tooltip all move together via one _siteHhmm, so the widget can never label its axis in one zone and its chips in another; the clock is captured in build (the axis/tooltip callbacks run during layout, where ref.watch is illegal, and ref.read would freeze the faces on the pre-settings-resolution SystemClock — which is exactly how the first attempt at this failed). The astronomy is deliberately untouched: nowOverride/DateTime.now() still supply the true instant. (3) target_preview_tooltip.dart — the sequencer's 'Transit: HH:MM' line. SystemClock.fromUtc is toLocal(), so every rig on 'use system time' renders byte-identically to before.
test: Three new files, each pumping the PRODUCTION widget through the real app_settings -> clockProvider graph under two zones. tonight_tab_timezone_test.dart -> 'twilight and moon faces follow the chosen site timezone' (sunset pinned 20:14Z renders 05:14 under UTC+09:00, and 20:14 is absent) + 'a site on UTC reads the UTC faces'. altitude_chart_timezone_test.dart -> 'the rise/transit/set faces follow the chosen site timezone' (same solve under UTC and UTC+09:00; asserts each chip moves by exactly 9h mod 24h, i.e. the FACE moved and the SOLVE did not). target_preview_tooltip_timezone_test.dart -> 'the transit line follows the chosen site timezone' + 'a site on UTC reads the UTC transit'. 18/18 green together with the pre-existing observing_site_gating_test.dart and night_context_chip_timezone_test.dart.
revert_check: Each production call site severed on its own. (1) tonight_tab.dart:110 `final clock = ref.watch(clockProvider);` -> `const clock = SystemClock();` — both tonight-tab cases FAILED. (2) altitude_chart.dart:305 `_clock = ref.watch(clockProvider);` -> `_clock = const SystemClock();` — the chart case FAILED with 'UTC 12:01 vs UTC+09:00 12:01'. (3) target_preview_tooltip.dart:343 `ref.watch(clockProvider)` -> `const SystemClock()` — both tooltip cases FAILED. All three restored -> 18/18 pass.
caveats: FixedOffsetClock is a fixed offset with no DST rule (pre-existing, stated in the Timezone row's own subtitle). Timestamps outside these surfaces — FITS headers, log lines, analytics chart axes — remain host-local; pre-existing and unchanged by this wave. The chart test had to key its ProviderScope by timezone: without the key Flutter updates the existing scope in place, the first zone's resolved AppSettingsState survives, and both pumps report the same face whether the fix is present or not — a test that could only pass. Full skotiq_app suite as the gate runs it (`flutter test --exclude-tags golden`): 2818/2818 green; dart analyze and dart format clean on all changed files.

title: The 'Maximum Quality' integration profile is a placebo -- it produces byte-identical settings to Balanced
summary: Closed before this wave (the finding's verdict quotes an older source). integration_settings.dart:754-757 now returns ransacThresholdPx 1.0 (vs the 2.0 default at :673), maxRefStars 120 (vs 60 at :674) and NormalizationMode.local (vs global at :681) — three knobs that all cost real work, none of them a restatement of a default. Not a label-only change: toBridgeSettings() puts ransacThresholdPx/maxRefStars in the native `align` block and the normalization mode in `normalization` (integration_settings.dart:946-963), the two service callers that reach native both send it (post_session_integration_service.dart:290 and :417, master_accumulation_service.dart:162), and the Rust side consumes it — post_session.rs:1764-1768 copies ransac_threshold_px and max_ref_stars into the registration config, which registration.rs:323/705 uses as the RANSAC inlier gate. The panel's readout is also no longer identical across profiles: integration_settings_panel.dart:33-68 derives the chip list by DIFFING against Balanced rather than hand-writing a blurb per preset, so it cannot claim a distinction a profile does not make.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/session_review/integration_settings_panel_test.dart -> 'no two integration profiles produce the same stack' (compares every preset's toBridgeSettings() payload pairwise — the strongest form, since it is the native payload not the Dart object), 'Maximum Quality actually costs something over Balanced', and 'the readout names the knobs the active profile changes'. 9/9 in that file, 26/26 in skotiq_core integration_settings_test.dart.
revert_check: Reverted the preset body at integration_settings.dart:754-757 back to `const IntegrationSettings(sourcePreset: IntegrationPreset.maximumQuality)` (all-defaults, i.e. byte-identical to Balanced). THREE tests FAILED: 'no two integration profiles produce the same stack', 'Maximum Quality actually costs something over Balanced', 'the readout names the knobs the active profile changes' ('Found 0 widgets with text containing RANSAC 1.0 px'). Restored -> 9/9 pass.
caveats: The one-line prose summary ('Will integrate N accepted subs using Winsorized sigma...') is still the same sentence for Balanced and Maximum Quality, because neither changes the rejection algorithm or the cull fraction. The differing knobs are named in the chip row directly beneath it, so the panel as a whole no longer describes the two runs identically.

title: Confirming a First Light candidate does not update the Observing Alerts tab beside it
summary: Closed before this wave. The root cause was that the alert surfaces read the transientAlertStatesProvider override map bare and fell back to newAlert on a miss, throwing away what the detection row already knew. transient_alert_provider.dart:924-928 now defines `resolveTransientAlertState(alert, overrides) => overrides[alert.id] ?? alert.state`, and EVERY surface that renders or filters an alert goes through it: transients_screen.dart:180 (the card) and :213/:219/:225 (the New/Queued/Observed filters), suggestions transient_alerts_panel.dart:131 and :206-207 (render + sort), status-bar transient_alert_badge.dart:444 (the dropdown), and unacknowledged AlertCountProvider at transient_alert_provider.dart:941-950 (the bell count). transient_alert_mapper.dart:66-70 maps reviewed -> acknowledged, and the list is live: activeTransientAlertsProvider re-merges on the drift watch query (transient_alert_provider.dart:552-556 listening to allTransientDetectionsProvider, transient_detections_provider.dart:94-99).
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/transients/transients_confirmed_state_test.dart -> 'a confirmed detection is not badged New on Observing Alerts' + 'a confirmed detection does not sit under the New filter'; packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/transients/alert_state_across_surfaces_test.dart -> the same claim for the suggestions panel and the status-bar dropdown, each with a still-New counterpart so the assertion is not vacuous. 12/12 in test/screens/transients/.
revert_check: TWO reverts. (1) The shared resolver, transient_alert_provider.dart:928 `overrides[alert.id] ?? alert.state` -> `overrides[alert.id] ?? TransientAlertState.newAlert`: 4 tests FAILED across all three surfaces. (2) The production call site, transients_screen.dart:180 `resolveTransientAlertState(alert, states)` -> `states[alert.id]`: both transients_confirmed_state_test cases FAILED. Restored -> 12/12 pass.
caveats: DELIBERATE NON-CHANGE, recorded so it is not mistaken for an oversight: the reverse direction is not wired. Dismissing a First-Light-sourced alert on Observing Alerts writes only the override row, so First Light still lists the candidate as un-triaged. I did not write through, because the two Dismiss actions do not mean the same thing — First Light's tooltip is 'Dismiss artefact' and its toast is 'Dismissed as an artefact - it will not resurface', and it feeds dismissedTileSignatures, which suppresses FUTURE detections at that sky position. Silently upgrading 'hide this alert' into 'never tell me about this patch of sky again' could bury a real transient; the symmetric write on acknowledge would be worse still, since reviewed=true is what admits a candidate to the curated TNS/AAVSO submit list (transient_candidate_card.dart:385). That is a product decision, not a bug fix.
